purpose: Guide a broad new-product or minimum viable product specification across activated capabilities, with testable requirements, explicit deferred scope, telemetry, and operational release controls.

ordered_sections.title: Document control and status
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify ownership, version, lifecycle state, and approval status.

ordered_sections.title: Stakeholder and business source requirements
ordered_sections.purpose: Record the authoritative needs that drive the product definition.

ordered_sections.title: Terminology
ordered_sections.purpose: Define stable product, customer, system, state, and measurement terms.

ordered_sections.title: Problem, value, and evidence
ordered_sections.purpose: Explain the observed need, affected outcomes, and evidence supporting the product investment.

ordered_sections.title: Objectives, success conditions, and non-goals
ordered_sections.purpose: Define intended outcomes and explicit boundaries for the minimum viable scope.

ordered_sections.title: Scope, personas, and eligibility
ordered_sections.purpose: Identify supported actors, contexts, entry conditions, and excluded scope.

ordered_sections.title: Use cases and current and proposed flows
ordered_sections.purpose: Describe numbered use cases and observable end-to-end behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Activated capability modules
ordered_sections.purpose: Define the objective, flow, requirements, acceptance, telemetry, dependencies, failure behavior, and deferred scope for each activated capability.

ordered_sections.title: Functional and non-functional requirements
ordered_sections.purpose: Specify atomic, necessary, prioritized, traceable, and verifiable behavior.

ordered_sections.title: Acceptance, test scenarios, and traceability
ordered_sections.purpose: Connect source needs, use cases, requirements, scenarios, and verification evidence.

ordered_sections.title: Metrics, telemetry, and data quality
ordered_sections.purpose: Define success measures, instrumentation, ownership, and behavior when data is incomplete or inconsistent.

ordered_sections.title: Edge, error, accessibility, and failure behavior
ordered_sections.purpose: Specify observable behavior outside the primary success path.

ordered_sections.title: Dependencies, risks, assumptions, and tenets
ordered_sections.purpose: Expose conditions, ownership, mitigations, and principles that affect delivery.

ordered_sections.title: Verification method and stakeholder sign-off
ordered_sections.purpose: Assign verification methods, reviewers, and approval state.

ordered_sections.title: Rollout, rollback, and operational ownership
ordered_sections.purpose: Define staged release, recovery, support, and accountable operational ownership.

narrative_rules: Derive requirements from authoritative source needs through numbered use cases.
Add a requirement only when an existing requirement does not cover a valid use case.
Keep every requirement singular, observable, necessary or explicitly optional, prioritized, and verifiable.
Separate stakeholder-driven behavior from implementation or system-design constraints.
Organize broad scope into activated capability modules rather than one undifferentiated requirement list.
For each activated module, state its objective, flow, requirements, acceptance, telemetry, dependencies, failure behavior, and deferred scope.
Make minimum viable boundaries and deferred capabilities explicit.
Describe customer or business value before detailed implementation behavior.
Include negative, boundary, accessibility, error, and recovery behavior where applicable.
evidence_rules: Trace material claims to approved sources or visibly labeled assumptions.
For every metric, retain its definition, population, period, grain, comparator, source, freshness, and caveat.
Keep observations, targets, forecasts, assumptions, and commitments in separate evidence states.
Define instrumentation and data-quality behavior for every activated capability where measurement is required.
Do not infer acceptance, telemetry, or release readiness from source silence.
Record deferred scope as a decision, not as an implied future commitment.
terminology_rules: Use stable identifiers for source needs, use cases, requirements, acceptance criteria, tests, metrics, dependencies, and capability modules.
Use one defined term for each actor, product object, state, flow, and outcome.
Distinguish minimum viable scope, deferred scope, non-goals, dependencies, and later possibilities.
Expand acronyms at first use unless an approved glossary marks them as established.
formatting_rules: Number use cases, requirements, acceptance criteria, test scenarios, metrics, and dependencies for traceability.
Use a repeatable module structure only for activated capabilities, without creating empty sections for inactive capabilities.
Use tables for traceability, dictionaries, state behavior, and aligned comparisons.
Keep rationale and causal reasoning in prose.
Show lifecycle and approval state for requirements and release decisions.
Apply the current organization template before default product-document formatting.
hard_fail_rules: Block publication when an activated capability lacks its objective, flow, requirements, acceptance, telemetry, dependencies, failure behavior, or deferred scope.
Block publication when a requirement is compound, ambiguous, unobservable, unnecessary, or unverifiable.
Block publication when traceability from source need through verification is missing.
Block publication when rollout lacks rollback and operational ownership.
Block publication when evidence is fabricated, untraceable, mislabeled, or missing critical context.
Block publication when body text and tables conflict or a material contradiction remains unresolved.
Block publication when a date, owner, target, fact, or commitment is silently introduced.
Block publication when required overview context is absent without an approved exception.
Block publication when source-specific sample facts appear in a new artifact.
Block publication when language repair changes a requirement, decision, or protected fact.
Block any full-language-conformance status unless the configured bundle, checks, exceptions, and human review are approved.

source_manifest.reference: Supplied new-product and minimum viable product reference
